prerequisites.text: Anyone born after January 1, 1972 must show proof of hunter education before buying a first Washington hunting license (a one-time deferral is available).
prerequisites.quote: Prior to purchasing their first Washington state hunting license, all individuals born after January 1, 1972 must show proof that they have completed a hunter education class.

prerequisites.text: Deer and elk: buy the hunting license and pick the transport tag (weapon and area) that matches the hunt before you can buy a special permit application.
prerequisites.quote: You must select your transport tag, including hunt method and location, before you can purchase a special permit application.

prerequisites.text: Goat, moose and sheep: no license needed to apply; if drawn, pay for the license and tag by July 31 or the permit goes to an alternate.
prerequisites.quote: Hunting licenses for mountain goat, moose, or bighorn sheep do not have to be purchased unless you are selected for a special hunt permit.

prerequisites.text: Buy a separate application for each permit category (e.g., Quality Elk, Bull Elk, Antlerless Elk, Goat, Antlered Bull Moose, Sheep Any Ram). Up to 4 hunt choices per application, 2 for Quality deer and elk.
prerequisites.quote: You can apply for a maximum of four hunt choices per application, except in the quality deer and elk categories.

prerequisites.text: Goat, Antlered Bull Moose and Sheep Any Ram: once you report a harvest (or fail to report), you can never apply in that category again.
prerequisites.quote: If a hunter reports taking a mountain goat on one of these hunts, or fails to report their hunting activity, no further special hunt applications for "Goat" can be purchased.

prerequisites.text: Multi-season deer/elk: no license needed to apply; if drawn, buy the multi-season tag (plus a deer or elk license) by midnight July 31, 2027.
prerequisites.quote: You DO NOT need to purchase a deer or elk license and tag before purchasing a multi-season application.

notes: 2027 special hunt permit dates (deer, elk, goat, moose, sheep) are not posted yet; WDFW publishes them in the 2027 pamphlet, usually in April. The 2026 window is recorded as last_year: the pamphlet said 'April 20 through midnight on May 20, 2026', then WDFW extended submission to May 27 (news release updated May 14, 2026). The extended deadline's time of day was not restated, so it is date-only. Applications were already on sale before April 20 ('applications are for sale now' on April 13), but the sale start date is not stated. resultsBy 2026-06-30 reflects the pamphlet's 'available by the end of June'. The 2027 multi-season deer/elk drawing dates ARE published in the 2026 pamphlet (p. 14); no time of day is given for the March 31 deadline, and results come only 'In April'. Fees are the 2026 license-year schedule (April 1, 2026 - March 31, 2027), pamphlet p. 8; online and phone card purchases add a 2.9% fee. No separate nonresident quota was found in the pamphlet, and no WDFW quote rules one out. Washington has no pronghorn season, so ANTELOPE is not included.
